steps.prompt: A $5$ m ladder leans against a wall with its foot $3$ m from the wall. How high up the wall does it reach? How could you be sure without measuring?

cards.title: Pythagoras
cards.body: In a right triangle with legs $a$ and $b$ and hypotenuse $c$ (the side opposite the right angle), $a^2 + b^2 = c^2$. Know the common triples and their multiples: $3, 4, 5$; $5, 12, 13$; $8, 15, 17$; $7, 24, 25$.

cards.title: Worked example: the hypotenuse
cards.problem: A right triangle has legs $9$ and $12$. How long is the hypotenuse?

cards.title: Special right triangles
cards.body: A $45^\circ$-$45^\circ$-$90^\circ$ triangle has sides $x, x, x\sqrt{2}$: half a square, cut along its diagonal. A $30^\circ$-$60^\circ$-$90^\circ$ triangle has sides $x, x\sqrt{3}, 2x$: half an equilateral triangle. So an equilateral triangle with side $s$ has height $\frac{s\sqrt{3}}{2}$ and area $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}s^2$.

cards.title: Worked example: an equilateral triangle
cards.problem: An equilateral triangle has side $6$. What is its height?

steps.text: The height cuts the base in half.

try.prompt: How long is each half of the base?

steps.text: The height is $\sqrt{6^2 - 3^2} = \sqrt{27} = 3\sqrt{3}$. Type roots like 3√3.

cards.title: The common trap: the wrong side or adding legs
cards.body: The hypotenuse is always the longest side, opposite the right angle: to find a leg, subtract, $b^2 = c^2 - a^2$. And $a^2 + b^2$ is not $(a + b)^2$: you can't just add the legs.

prompts: Which Pythagorean triples do you know by heart now?
